title: Breaking with Trump, Jensen Huang makes the case for immigration: 'We want all the world's great minds to come here'
key_facts: Huang, an immigrant from Taiwan, said on the Bg2 podcast the US should keep attracting top tech talent
He said immigrants must enter 'lawfully' but a good balance is needed
Trump signed an order in September 2025 setting a $100,000 fee for new H-1B applications
Last week Vance and officials banned Microsoft and Adobe from a programme linking H-1B visas to green cards
A White House spokeswoman said there is 'no shortage of American minds and hands'
Huang has been a reliable Trump ally and opposed new AI regulation last month
quote_evidence: "We want all the world's great minds to come here, bring their great ideas," Huang said on the Bg2 podcast.
Huang's spirited comments clash with the Trump administration's agenda, which has sought to crack down on H-1B visas.
why_it_matters_hint: A close Trump ally publicly breaks with the visa crackdown.
notes: Full text from fulltext file. Podcast date not stated; BI calls it 'recent'. It reacts to the administration's visa policy generally, including Vance's 8 Oct ban on Microsoft and Adobe from the green-card programme, but does not name a single earlier story.
